references.text: The goat as a sin offering is prescribed in the Mosaic Law for leaders who sin. Here the use of the goat as a sin offering is described.
A goat is used as a sin offering at the dedication of the tabernacle, which corresponds to the dedication offerings from the tribal leaders.
The first time in chapter 7 where the goat as a sin offering is mentioned, at Nahshon's offering. The same wording is used for all the tribal leaders' sin offerings.
Nathanal's offering includes the same sin offering with a goat, showing the consistent pattern in the dedication offerings.
A goat as a sin offering for the whole congregation when they sin unintentionally. Shows the goat as a sin offering in various contexts.
Monthly sin offering with a goat to the Lord, as part of the regular offerings in Israel.
During Hezekiah's reform, goats were sacrificed as sin offerings for the kingdom, the sanctuary, and Judah.
At the temple dedication after the exile, goats were sacrificed as sin offerings for all Israel, one for each tribe.
